answer: Named-Identity Cost Ledger: each agent identity must post a unique, externally verifiable artifact—an onyx hardware attestation key bound to a physical device—before its first transaction, and the kernel records that binding permanently. Cloning the identity forces a factory reset that voids the key, so a duplicate cannot reuse the haven of the original's reputation and pays a fresh attestation cost per clone. Because the ledger rejects any key already seen, marginal duplication yields zero transferable value while incurring full hardware and registration expense.
